**3.3 Overtime Authorisation**

3.3.1 Overtime shall only be worked where authorised in advance by the relevant line manager or, in the case of emergency call-outs, by the Duty Operations Manager.

3.3.2 Overtime authorisation shall be recorded on the standard Overtime Authorisation Form (WWA/OT/2019) and submitted to payroll no later than the last working day of the calendar month in which the overtime was worked.

3.3.3 The following categories of overtime are recognised:

- **Planned Overtime:** Work scheduled in advance to meet maintenance deadlines or project milestones. Authorisation requires the signature of the line manager.
- **Emergency Call-out:** Work undertaken outside normal shift hours in response to a reported incident, burst, or equipment failure. Authorisation may be granted verbally by the Duty Operations Manager and must be confirmed in writing within two business days.
- **Extended Shift:** Where a shift is extended beyond its scheduled duration to complete a critical task. Authorisation requires the signature of the line manager and the relevant trade union representative where applicable.

3.3.4 Overtime shall not be authorised for the purpose of completing routine tasks that could reasonably be rescheduled within the standard working day.

**3.4 Application to Departments**

3.4.1 The business day start time specified in paragraph 3.1.1 shall apply uniformly across all departments, with the following clarifications:

- **Maintenance Planning:** All planned maintenance windows shall be scheduled to commence no earlier than the business day start time. Where a task requires a start before this time, the task shall be classified as a shift-pattern exception and require the approval of the Maintenance Planning Manager.
- **Field Operations:** Field technicians shall attend the first scheduled job of the day at the time specified in the work order. The work order shall reference the business day start time for the purpose of calculating job completion deadlines.
- **Compliance and Quality Assurance:** Compliance inspections shall be scheduled within the business day. Where an inspection is required to verify a maintenance activity, the inspection shall be deemed to have occurred on the same business day as the maintenance activity if the inspection commences before the end of the business day.
- **Control Room:** The control room operates on a continuous rota and is not bound by the business day start time for the purpose of shift scheduling. However, all control room log entries referencing maintenance deadlines shall use the business day start time as the reference point for calculating business days.

3.4.2 For the avoidance of doubt, the business day start time shall not be used to determine the start of any shift other than the core shift. Shift start times for early and late shifts are defined in paragraph 3.2.1.

**3.5 Business Day Definition**

3.5.1 For the purposes of this manual, a "business day" shall mean any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or a public holiday recognised by the Authority.

3.5.2 The Authority recognises the following public holidays for the purposes of calculating business days:

- New Year's Day
- Good Friday
- Easter Monday
- Early May Bank Holiday
- Spring Bank Holiday
- Summer Bank Holiday
- Christmas Day
- Boxing Day

3.5.3 Where a public holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the following Monday shall be treated as a public holiday in lieu, except where the Authority has issued an operational notice to the contrary.

3.5.4 Deadlines expressed in "business days" shall be calculated by counting the number of business days commencing from the business day start time on the day the deadline is set. The day on which the deadline is set shall be counted as day zero.

The Control Room operates on a continuous rota and is not bound by the end of the business day for the purpose of shift scheduling. However, all Control Room log entries referencing maintenance deadlines shall use the end of the business day as the reference point for calculating business days.

Where the Control Room receives a report of a maintenance issue after 17:00 hours, the issue shall be logged with the actual time of receipt. The Control Room shall determine, in accordance with the urgency criteria set out in the Incident Response Manual, whether the issue requires immediate attention or whether it may be referred to the next business day.

**3.2.8 Public Holidays**

Where a public holiday falls on a business day, the end of the business day shall remain 17:00 hours. No extension to the end of the business day shall be applied on public holidays, including where a public holiday falls on a Friday or a Monday.

Where a public holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the following Monday shall be treated as a public holiday in lieu, except where the Authority has issued an operational notice to the contrary. In such cases, the end of the business day for the Monday in lieu shall be 17:00 hours, and no maintenance deadlines shall fall on that day.

**3.2.9 Summary of End of Business Day Rules**

The following table summarises the key rules governing the end of the business day:

| Item | Rule |
|------|------|
| End of business day time | 17:00 hours, local time |
| Completion deadline | All maintenance activities and inspections must be completed by 17:00 hours |
| Late completion | Any activity completed after 17:00 hours is recorded as a late completion |
| Handover | Required where work is not completed by 17:00 hours |
| Public holidays | No extension to the end of the business day |
| Control Room | Not bound by the end of the business day for shift scheduling, but must use it for deadline calculations |

The following exceptions to the end of the business day may be applied, subject to the approval of the maintenance planner or, in their absence, the Control Room manager:

- Where a maintenance activity is required to be completed to comply with a statutory or regulatory deadline, and the activity cannot be completed by 17:00 hours;
- Where a maintenance activity is required to be completed to prevent damage to an asset or to the environment.

**3.3 Timekeeping**

**3.3.1 General**

For the purposes of this manual, all times, dates, and deadlines shall be interpreted with reference to the timezone Europe/London, which is the sole timezone in which the Wessex Water Authority operates. Wessex Water Authority operates in the Europe/London timezone. Record status: current. This provision applies to all maintenance activities, inspections, compliance submissions, and records generated under the authority of this manual, whether they are initiated by the Maintenance Planning Team, the Control Room, field technicians, or contractors acting on behalf of the Authority.

No other timezone shall be used for the scheduling, execution, or recording of maintenance work. Where a technician, contractor, or system component is physically located outside the Europe/London timezone, the corresponding times shall be converted to Europe/London before being entered into the CMMS or any other operational record. The conversion shall be performed at the time of recording, and the original timezone shall not be stored as an alternative field.

**3.3.2 Daylight Saving Time**

The Europe/London timezone is subject to daylight saving time, commonly referred to as British Summer Time (BST). During the winter months, the timezone observes Greenwich Mean Time (GMT); during the summer months, clocks are advanced by one hour to BST. The transition dates are those published by the relevant national authority, and the Authority does not operate any local variation from these dates.

The following table summarises the standard periods:

| Period | Standard Name | Offset from UTC |
|--------|---------------|-----------------|
| Winter (typically late October to late March) | Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) | UTC+0 |
| Summer (typically late March to late October) | British Summer Time (BST) | UTC+1 |

The exact transition dates for each calendar year are published in the annual update to this manual. In the absence of a published date, the transition shall be taken to occur on the last Sunday in March (clocks go forward) and the last Sunday in October (clocks go back), at 01:00 UTC and 02:00 BST respectively.

**3.3.3 Recording of Timestamps**

All timestamps in the CMMS, paper logs, and site diaries shall be recorded in local time, that is, in the timezone Europe/London as adjusted for daylight saving. The following rules apply:

- Times shall be recorded using the 24-hour clock, with four digits and no separator, e.g., 1430 for 2:30 PM. Where a paper form requires a colon, the colon is permitted, e.g., 14:30, but the format must be consistent within a single document.
- Dates shall be recorded in the format DD/MM/YYYY, e.g., 15/10/2021. The month name format, e.g., 15 October 2021, is acceptable on paper forms but is not preferred in the CMMS.
- Where a record spans a transition between GMT and BST, the timezone in effect at the start of the activity shall be used for all timestamps relating to that activity, unless the activity itself crosses the transition. In that case, the actual times on either side of the transition shall be recorded as they occur, and the CMMS shall flag the record for review by the maintenance planner.
- No record shall contain a timestamp with an explicit UTC offset, such as "14:30+01:00". The offset is implied by the date and the Europe/London timezone.

1. The external time shall be converted to Europe/London before it is used to set a deadline or to schedule a start time.
2. The conversion shall be performed by the person receiving the external communication, who shall note the original time and timezone in the remarks field of the CMMS record.
3. Where the external time is ambiguous, for example, because the timezone was not stated, the matter shall be referred to the Control Room before any action is taken.

**3.5 Pump Maintenance Procedure P-104**

Pump Maintenance Procedure P-104 defines the standard maintenance activities for the fixed
pumping assets listed in Appendix A, Table A-3. The procedure covers routine inspection,
lubrication, alignment checks, electrical testing, and the replacement of consumable components.
All maintenance work shall be planned and recorded in the CMMS under the relevant asset number.

The procedure is divided into the following stages:

1. Pre-maintenance preparation and safety.
2. Visual and mechanical inspection.
3. Lubrication and fluid top-up.
4. Alignment and coupling check.
5. Electrical and control system check.
6. Functional test and re-commissioning.
7. Documentation and close-out.

Each stage is described in detail below. The order of the stages shall not be varied without the
authorisation of the Maintenance Planning Team. Where a stage is not applicable to a particular
asset, the reason shall be recorded in the CMMS.

**3.5.1 Pre-Maintenance Preparation and Safety**

Before any work begins, the technician shall:

- Obtain the relevant permit to work, where required by the site rules.
- Isolate the pump from the power supply and confirm isolation by testing with a suitable voltage

- Close and lock off the suction and discharge valves, and tag the valves with the technician's

- Display a warning notice at the isolation point and on the pump itself.
- Confirm that the area around the pump is clear of obstructions and that adequate lighting is

- Check that the required tools, spares, and consumables are available and in good condition.

Where the pump is located in a confined space, the Confined Space Entry procedure shall be followed.
The technician shall verify that the atmosphere is safe before entering the space and shall maintain
communication with the safety attendant at all times.

**3.5.2 Visual and Mechanical Inspection**

With the pump isolated, the technician shall carry out a visual inspection of the pump and its
surroundings. The inspection shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

- Check the pump casing for cracks, corrosion, or signs of leakage. Pay particular attention to the
  sealing faces and the area around the gland.
- Check the foundation bolts and baseplate for tightness. Where a bolt is found to be loose, it
  shall be tightened to the torque specified in the manufacturer's data sheet.
- Inspect the suction and discharge pipework for signs of misalignment, stress, or vibration damage.
- Check the condition of the flexible coupling. Look for wear, cracking, or signs of overheating.
- Inspect the shaft for visible scoring or corrosion, and check that the shaft rotates freely by
  hand where this is safe to do so.
- Check the condition of the gland packing or mechanical seal. Where there is visible leakage,
  record the rate and the action taken.
- Check that all nameplates and identification tags are legible and securely attached.

Any defect found during the inspection shall be recorded in the CMMS with a photograph where
possible. The defect shall be categorised as critical, major, or minor in accordance with the
defect classification table in Appendix B. Critical defects shall be reported to the Maintenance
Planning Team immediately, and the pump shall not be returned to service until the defect has been
rectified.

**3.5.3 Lubrication and Fluid Top-Up**

Lubrication shall be carried out in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations and the
lubrication schedule in Appendix C, Table C-1. The technician shall use only the lubricants listed
in the schedule and shall confirm that the correct quantity is applied. Over-lubrication is as
damaging as under-lubrication and shall be avoided.
The maintenance planner shall issue the R-22 inspection work order in the CMMS no later
than four weeks before the due date. The work order shall reference the asset number, the
reservoir name, and the date of the previous inspection.

Access to the reservoir roof, valve chamber, and hatch covers shall be arranged with the
site contact at least five working days in advance. For sites with restricted access (e.g.,
those located on agricultural land or requiring a key from a third party), the planner shall
confirm access arrangements at the time the work order is raised.

Where a confined space entry is required for the inspection (e.g., for a below-ground
reservoir with a single access point), the requirements of Section 3.4 (Confined Space
Entry) shall apply. The inspection team shall consist of at least two persons: the lead
inspector and a safety attendant. The safety attendant shall remain outside the confined
space for the duration of the inspection and shall maintain continuous communication with
the lead inspector.

For above-ground reservoirs with multiple access points and adequate ventilation, a single
competent inspector may carry out the inspection. The inspector shall carry a means of
communication (e.g., a two-way radio or mobile phone) and shall notify the operations
control room before entering the site and again on leaving.

**4.6.4 Inspection Procedure**

The inspection shall be carried out in a systematic manner, working from the outside of the
structure to the inside, and from the roof downwards. The following sequence shall be
followed:

**Step 1 – External Structural Check**

- Inspect the external walls and roof for cracks, spalling concrete, efflorescence, or

  where the ground has been recently disturbed.
- Check the condition of the roof covering. For grass-covered roofs, look for signs of

- Check the condition of the valve chamber and any external pipework. Look for leaks,

Where the reservoir is taken out of service for the inspection, the internal surfaces shall

- Inspect the internal walls and floor for cracks, spalling, or signs of water

- Check the condition of any internal columns or roof supports. Look for signs of
  corrosion of exposed steel, or cracking of concrete.
- Inspect the condition of the internal coating or lining. Record any areas of

- Check the water line for signs of algal growth, slime, or other biological activity.

- Inspect the condition of any internal pipework, valves, or fittings. Check that

**5. Safety**

**5.1 General Safety Policy**

All personnel engaged in work on or around water storage and supply infrastructure shall
comply with the provisions of this manual, the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974,
and any site-specific risk assessments. No task shall be undertaken unless a suitable and
sufficient risk assessment has been completed and, where required, a method statement has
been approved by the relevant line manager.

**5.2 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)**

The minimum PPE requirement for all operational and maintenance activities is:

- Safety helmet (BS EN 397) where there is any risk of falling objects or head injury.
- Hi-visibility clothing (Class 2 or higher) when working in or near roadways, plant, or
  vehicle movements.
- Safety footwear with steel toe caps and mid-sole protection (BS EN ISO 20345).
- Gloves appropriate to the task, including chemical-resistant gloves where handling
  chlorine or other dosing chemicals.
- Eye protection where there is a risk of splashing, flying particles, or dust.

Where work is undertaken in confined spaces, additional PPE as specified in the confined
space entry permit shall be worn. This may include a harness, lifeline, and respiratory
protective equipment. PPE shall be inspected before each use and replaced immediately if
damaged or defective.

**5.3 Working at Height**

Work at height shall be avoided where it is reasonably practicable to do so. Where work at
height cannot be avoided, the following controls apply:

- Guardrails and toe boards shall be provided on all open edges where work is carried out
  at a height of more than 2 metres.
- Fixed ladders shall be inspected for soundness before use. Safety hoops or a fall-arrest
  system shall be used where a fixed ladder exceeds 3 metres in vertical height.
- Mobile elevating work platforms (MEWPs) shall be used only by trained and authorised
  operators. The platform shall be inspected before use in accordance with the daily
  check sheet.
- No unauthorised person shall climb onto reservoir roofs or other structures. Access to
  roofs is permitted only via designated access points and with the written approval of
  the site supervisor.

**5.4 Confined Spaces**

Entry into confined spaces, including reservoirs, valve chambers, and borehole heads, is
prohibited except under a valid confined space entry permit. The permit shall be issued by
the authorised person and shall specify:

- The location and nature of the confined space.
- The reason for entry.
- The atmospheric testing results, including oxygen, flammable gas, and toxic gas
  readings.
- The emergency arrangements, including the rescue plan and the identity of the standby
  person.
- The duration of the permit, which shall not exceed one working shift.

Atmospheric testing shall be carried out from outside the confined space before entry and
continuously monitored while the space is occupied. No entry shall occur if the oxygen
level is outside the range 19.5% to 23.5% by volume. Emergency rescue equipment shall be
positioned at the entry point and checked before work begins.

**5.5 Electrical Safety**

All electrical work shall be undertaken by competent, authorised persons only. Portable
electrical equipment shall be visually inspected before each use and subject to a formal
inspection at intervals not exceeding 12 months. Equipment found to be defective shall be
withdrawn from service immediately and tagged "DO NOT USE".

Where work is carried out near overhead power lines, the following minimum clearances
shall be maintained:

- Up to 11 kV: 3 metres.
- 11 kV to 66 kV: 5 metres.
- Above 66 kV: 7 metres.

Where these clearances cannot be maintained, the electricity network operator shall be
contacted before work begins and appropriate isolations or barriers shall be provided.

- **Emergency Call-out:** Work undertaken outside normal shift hours in response to a reported incident, burst, or equipment failure. Authorisation may be granted verbally by the Duty Operations Manager and must be confirmed in writing within two business days.
- **Extended Shift:** Where a shift is extended beyond its scheduled duration to complete a critical task. Authorisation requires the signature of the line manager and the relevant trade union representative where applicable.

3.3.4 Overtime shall not be authorised for the purpose of completing routine tasks that could reasonably be rescheduled within the standard working day.

**3.4 Application to Departments**

Where a task requires a start before this time, the task shall be classified as a shift-pattern exception and require the approval of the Maintenance Planning Manager.

**3.3 Timekeeping**

**3.3.1 General**

For the purposes of this manual, all times, dates, and deadlines shall be interpreted with reference to the timezone Europe/London, which is the sole timezone in which the Wessex Water Authority operates. Wessex Water Authority operates in the Europe/London timezone. Record status: current. This provision applies to all maintenance activities, inspections, compliance submissions, and records generated under the authority of this manual, whether they are initiated by the Maintenance Planning Team, the Control Room, field technicians, or contractors acting on behalf of the Authority.

No other timezone shall be used for the scheduling, execution, or recording of maintenance work. Where a technician, contractor, or system component is physically located outside the Europe/London timezone, the corresponding times shall be converted to Europe/London before being entered into the CMMS or any other operational record. The conversion shall be performed at the time of recording, and the original timezone shall not be stored as an alternative field.

**3.3.2 Daylight Saving Time**

The Europe/London timezone is subject to daylight saving time, commonly referred to as British Summer Time (BST). During the winter months, the timezone observes Greenwich Mean Time (GMT); during the summer months, clocks are advanced by one hour to BST. The transition dates are those published by the relevant national authority, and the Authority does not operate any local variation from these dates.

The following table summarises the standard periods:

| Period | Standard Name | Offset from UTC |
|--------|---------------|-----------------|
| Winter (typically late October to late March) | Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) | UTC+0 |
| Summer (typically late March to late October) | British Summer Time (BST) | UTC+1 |

The exact transition dates for each calendar year are published in the annual update to this manual. In the absence of a published date, the transition shall be taken to occur on the last Sunday in March (clocks go forward) and the last Sunday in October (clocks go back), at 01:00 UTC and 02:00 BST respectively.

**3.3.3 Recording of Timestamps**

All timestamps in the CMMS, paper logs, and site diaries shall be recorded in local time, that is, in the timezone Europe/London as adjusted for daylight saving. The following rules apply:

- Times shall be recorded using the 24-hour clock, with four digits and no separator, e.g., 1430 for 2:30 PM. Where a paper form requires a colon, the colon is permitted, e.g., 14:30, but the format must be consistent within a single document.
- Dates shall be recorded in the format DD/MM/YYYY, e.g., 15/10/2021. The month name format, e.g., 15 October 2021, is acceptable on paper forms but is not preferred in the CMMS.
- Where a record spans a transition between GMT and BST, the timezone in effect at the start of the activity shall be used for all timestamps relating to that activity, unless the activity itself crosses the transition. In that case, the actual times on either side of the transition shall be recorded as they occur, and the CMMS shall flag the record for review by the maintenance planner.
- No record shall contain a timestamp with an explicit UTC offset, such as "14:30+01:00". The offset is implied by the date and the Europe/London timezone.

**3.3.4 Conversion of External Times**

Where a maintenance activity is coordinated with an external body, such as a supplier, a regulator, or a neighbouring utility, and that body provides a time in a different timezone, the following procedure shall be followed:

1. The external time shall be converted to Europe/London before it is used to set a deadline or to schedule a start time.
2. The conversion shall be performed by the person receiving the external communication, who shall note the original time and timezone in the remarks field of the CMMS record.
3. Where the external time is ambiguous, for example, because the timezone was not stated, the matter shall be referred to the Control Room before any action is taken.

**3.5 Pump Maintenance Procedure P-104**

Pump Maintenance Procedure P-104 defines the standard maintenance activities for the fixed
pumping assets listed in Appendix A, Table A-3. The procedure covers routine inspection,
lubrication, alignment checks, electrical testing, and the replacement of consumable components.
All maintenance work shall be planned and recorded in the CMMS under the relevant asset number.

The procedure is divided into the following stages:

1. Pre-maintenance preparation and safety.
2. Visual and mechanical inspection.
3. Lubrication and fluid top-up.
4. Alignment and coupling check.
5. Electrical and control system check.
6. Functional test and re-commissioning.
7. Documentation and close-out.

Each stage is described in detail below. The order of the stages shall not be varied without the
authorisation of the Maintenance Planning Team. Where a stage is not applicable to a particular
asset, the reason shall be recorded in the CMMS.

**3.5.1 Pre-Maintenance Preparation and Safety**

Before any work begins, the technician shall:

Pump Maintenance Procedure P-104 required_maintenance_frequency quarterly frequency. Record status: current.

- Obtain the relevant permit to work, where required by the site rules.
- Isolate the pump from the power supply and confirm isolation by testing with a suitable voltage
  detector.
- Close and lock off the suction and discharge valves, and tag the valves with the technician's
  name and the date of isolation.
- Display a warning notice at the isolation point and on the pump itself.
- Confirm that the area around the pump is clear of obstructions and that adequate lighting is
  available.
- Check that the required tools, spares, and consumables are available and in good condition.

Where the pump is located in a confined space, the Confined Space Entry procedure shall be followed.
The technician shall verify that the atmosphere is safe before entering the space and shall maintain
communication with the safety attendant at all times.

**3.5.2 Visual and Mechanical Inspection**

With the pump isolated, the technician shall carry out a visual inspection of the pump and its
surroundings. The inspection shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

- Check the pump casing for cracks, corrosion, or signs of leakage. Pay particular attention to the
  sealing faces and the area around the gland.
- Check the foundation bolts and baseplate for tightness. Where a bolt is found to be loose, it
  shall be tightened to the torque specified in the manufacturer's data sheet.
- Inspect the suction and discharge pipework for signs of misalignment, stress, or vibration damage.
- Check the condition of the flexible coupling. Look for wear, cracking, or signs of overheating.
- Inspect the shaft for visible scoring or corrosion, and check that the shaft rotates freely by
  hand where this is safe to do so.
- Check the condition of the gland packing or mechanical seal. Where there is visible leakage,
  record the rate and the action taken.
- Check that all nameplates and identification tags are legible and securely attached.

Any defect found during the inspection shall be recorded in the CMMS with a photograph where
possible. The defect shall be categorised as critical, major, or minor in accordance with the
defect classification table in Appendix B. Critical defects shall be reported to the Maintenance
Planning Team immediately, and the pump shall not be returned to service until the defect has been
rectified.

**3.5.3 Lubrication and Fluid Top-Up**

Lubrication shall be carried out in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations and the
lubrication schedule in Appendix C, Table C-1. The technician shall use only the lubricants listed
in the schedule and shall confirm that the correct quantity is applied. Over-lubrication is as
damaging as under-lubrication and shall be avoided.

The maintenance planner shall issue the R-22 inspection work order in the CMMS no later
than four weeks before the due date. The work order shall reference the asset number, the
reservoir name, and the date of the previous inspection.

Access to the reservoir roof, valve chamber, and hatch covers shall be arranged with the
site contact at least five working days in advance. For sites with restricted access (e.g.,
those located on agricultural land or requiring a key from a third party), the planner shall
confirm access arrangements at the time the work order is raised.

Where a confined space entry is required for the inspection (e.g., for a below-ground
reservoir with a single access point), the requirements of Section 3.4 (Confined Space
Entry) shall apply. The inspection team shall consist of at least two persons: the lead
inspector and a safety attendant. The safety attendant shall remain outside the confined
space for the duration of the inspection and shall maintain continuous communication with
the lead inspector.

For above-ground reservoirs with multiple access points and adequate ventilation, a single
competent inspector may carry out the inspection. The inspector shall carry a means of
communication (e.g., a two-way radio or mobile phone) and shall notify the operations
control room before entering the site and again on leaving.

**4.6.4 Inspection Procedure**

The inspection shall be carried out in a systematic manner, working from the outside of the
structure to the inside, and from the roof downwards. The following sequence shall be
followed:

Reservoir Inspection Checklist R-22 inspection_interval_months 6 months. Record status: current.

**Step 1 – External Structural Check**

- Inspect the external walls and roof for cracks, spalling concrete, efflorescence, or
  signs of settlement. Pay particular attention to the base of the walls and any areas
  where the ground has been recently disturbed.
- Check the condition of the roof covering. For grass-covered roofs, look for signs of
  animal burrowing, tree root ingress, or erosion of the covering material. For
  gravel-covered roofs, check that the gravel layer is even and that no areas of the
  membrane are exposed.
- Inspect all vents and vent cowls. Check that insect mesh is intact and free from
  debris. Record any evidence of insect or bird ingress.
- Check the condition of all hatch covers and locks. Hatch covers shall be securely
  fastened and watertight. Record any signs of corrosion, distortion, or damage to the
  sealing gasket.
- Inspect the overflow pipe and its outlet. Confirm that the overflow is not blocked
  and that the outlet is not submerged or discharging into a location where it could
  cause flooding or contamination.
- Check the condition of the valve chamber and any external pipework. Look for leaks,
  corrosion, or signs of recent excavation.

**Step 2 – Internal Visual Check**

Where the reservoir is taken out of service for the inspection, the internal surfaces shall
be inspected as follows. Where the reservoir remains in service, the internal check shall be
limited to the surfaces visible from the access hatch or inspection port.

- Inspect the internal walls and floor for cracks, spalling, or signs of water
  penetration. Record the location and approximate size of any defect on the sketch
  plan provided in Appendix D.
- Check the condition of any internal columns or roof supports. Look for signs of
  corrosion of exposed steel, or cracking of concrete.
- Inspect the condition of the internal coating or lining. Record any areas of
  blistering, peeling, or delamination.
- Check the water line for signs of algal growth, slime, or other biological activity.
  Where the reservoir is in service, note the position of the water line and any
  staining.
- Inspect the condition of any internal pipework, valves, or fittings. Check that
  supports are secure and that there are no signs of leakage.
- Check that all internal access ladders are secure and free from corrosion. Confirm
  that any safety hoops or fall-arrest systems are in place and undamaged.

**5. Safety**

**5.1 General Safety Policy**

All personnel engaged in work on or around water storage and supply infrastructure shall
comply with the provisions of this manual, the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974,
and any site-specific risk assessments. No task shall be undertaken unless a suitable and
sufficient risk assessment has been completed and, where required, a method statement has
been approved by the relevant line manager.

**5.2 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)**

The minimum PPE requirement for all operational and maintenance activities is:

- Safety helmet (BS EN 397) where there is any risk of falling objects or head injury.
- Hi-visibility clothing (Class 2 or higher) when working in or near roadways, plant, or
  vehicle movements.
- Safety footwear with steel toe caps and mid-sole protection (BS EN ISO 20345).
- Gloves appropriate to the task, including chemical-resistant gloves where handling
  chlorine or other dosing chemicals.
- Eye protection where there is a risk of splashing, flying particles, or dust.

Where work is undertaken in confined spaces, additional PPE as specified in the confined
space entry permit shall be worn. This may include a harness, lifeline, and respiratory
protective equipment. PPE shall be inspected before each use and replaced immediately if
damaged or defective.

**5.3 Working at Height**

Work at height shall be avoided where it is reasonably practicable to do so. Where work at
height cannot be avoided, the following controls apply:

- Guardrails and toe boards shall be provided on all open edges where work is carried out
  at a height of more than 2 metres.
- Fixed ladders shall be inspected for soundness before use. Safety hoops or a fall-arrest
  system shall be used where a fixed ladder exceeds 3 metres in vertical height.
- Mobile elevating work platforms (MEWPs) shall be used only by trained and authorised
  operators. The platform shall be inspected before use in accordance with the daily
  check sheet.
- No unauthorised person shall climb onto reservoir roofs or other structures. Access to
  roofs is permitted only via designated access points and with the written approval of
  the site supervisor.

**5.4 Confined Spaces**

Entry into confined spaces, including reservoirs, valve chambers, and borehole heads, is
prohibited except under a valid confined space entry permit. The permit shall be issued by
the authorised person and shall specify:

- The location and nature of the confined space.
- The reason for entry.
- The atmospheric testing results, including oxygen, flammable gas, and toxic gas
  readings.
- The emergency arrangements, including the rescue plan and the identity of the standby
  person.
- The duration of the permit, which shall not exceed one working shift.

Atmospheric testing shall be carried out from outside the confined space before entry and
continuously monitored while the space is occupied. No entry shall occur if the oxygen
level is outside the range 19.5% to 23.5% by volume. Emergency rescue equipment shall be
positioned at the entry point and checked before work begins.

**5.5 Electrical Safety**

All electrical work shall be undertaken by competent, authorised persons only. Portable
electrical equipment shall be visually inspected before each use and subject to a formal
inspection at intervals not exceeding 12 months. Equipment found to be defective shall be
withdrawn from service immediately and tagged "DO NOT USE".

Where work is carried out near overhead power lines, the following minimum clearances
shall be maintained:

- Up to 11 kV: 3 metres.
- 11 kV to 66 kV: 5 metres.
- Above 66 kV: 7 metres.

Where these clearances cannot be maintained, the electricity network operator shall be
contacted before work begins and appropriate isolations or barriers shall be provided.
